data.text:
Meet Li, your friendLi neighbor 🤝

There are people who would like Filipinos to believe that when a neighbor comes to knock on their door, a threat is to come. That every bridge is a trap, every donation a scheme, and acts of friendship, a geopolitical conspiracy. It is a worldview that festers on fear, selective memory, and the constant need to manufacture enemies where cooperation could easily exist.

When traffic in Manila and Davao was eased through the Binondo–Intramuros Bridge and the Bucana Bridge with the help of Chinese support, ordinary families did not stop to ask which political commentator or self-styled security expert had objections. They simply got home faster. Lesser traffic. When the pandemic brought fear and uncertainty, China delivered more that 55 million doses of vaccine. When typhoons and earthquakes hit communities, China sent rice, fertilizers by the tonnes, and cash aid by the millions. In moments of crises, what mattered was not rhetoric, but who actually showed up.

That is what neighbors do. They help. They build. And amidst these smear campaigns, will continue to do so.
